t: This Act shall affect only such right, title, and interest of the United States of America in and to the lands described in section 1 hereof as may have been retained by the United States of America, in fee simple, as a reversionary interest, or otherwise, under the Acts of March 30, 1822 (3 Stat. 659), March 2, 1827 (4 Stat. 234), and March 2, 1833 (4 Stat. 662), and as has not been disposed of, prior to the approval of this Act, by the United States of America.

fable.w: This section only limits the scope of the Act to whatever land interest the United States retained under earlier statutes and has not already disposed of. One might be tempted to read the mention of land interests as implicating outside parties such as a state or grantees, but the text provides no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: This Act shall affect only such right, title, and interest of the United States of America in and to the lands described in section 1 hereof

qwen_block.w: This section defines the scope of federal land interests affected by the Act. It contains no provisions for consultation, coordination, public comment, hearings, or advisory committees involving parties outside the federal government. It is purely a statement of legal scope regarding property rights.
qwen_block.s: This Act shall affect only such right, title, and interest of the United States of America in and to the lands described in section 1 hereof as may have been retained by the United States of America, in fee simple, as a reversionary interest, or otherwise, under the Acts of March 30, 1822 (3 Stat. 659), March 2, 1827 (4 Stat. 234), and March 2, 1833 (4 Stat. 662), and as has not been disposed of, prior to the approval of this Act, by the United States of America.

opus.w: This section only limits how far a land conveyance reaches: it covers whatever reversionary or other interest the United States kept under the 1822, 1827 and 1833 Acts and has not already disposed of. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Words like "right, title, and interest" may sound procedural, but they describe property rights, not anyone taking part in a federal decision.
opus.s: This Act shall affect only such right, title, and interest of the United States of America in and to the lands described in section 1 hereof as may have been retained by the United States of America

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the scope of federal property interests affected by the Act. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. The text is purely declarative regarding federal land rights.
qwen_chat.s: This Act shall affect only such right, title, and interest of the United States of America in and to the lands described in section 1 hereof as may have been retained by the United States of America, in fee simple, as a reversionary interest, or otherwise, under the Acts of March 30, 1822 (3 Stat. 659), March 2, 1827 (4 Stat. 234), and March 2, 1833 (4 Stat. 662), and as has not been disposed of, prior to the approval of this Act, by the United States of America.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Act affects rights in land, it implicitly involves consultation with landowners or local governments. However, the text itself contains no procedural requirement for such consultation; it merely defines the scope of federal property interests affected.
